Build the provider reports and issues CSVs of a saved run

Source: R/report_build.R
gpq_build_reports.Rd

Builds one HTML report and one issues CSV for each report unit of a run, from its results and never from its data, and writes them into the run's saved folder: reports/<unit>.html and tables/<unit>_issues.csv. Each unit's files hold only what that unit may see.

Usage

gpq_build_reports(
  results,
  output_dir,
  group_cols = NULL,
  lineage = NULL,
  lang = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  row_cap = NULL,
  example_cap = NULL,
  cell_cap = NULL
)

Arguments

results

A gpq_results object, such as gpq_check_conformance() returns, its issues classed by gpq_classify_issues() and its run written to output_dir by gpq_write_results().

output_dir

The folder that holds the run's folder, as given to gpq_write_results().

group_cols

NULL for the run's own group columns, or the run's report-unit column followed by any of its other group columns, which choose the breakdowns the reports show. For a run with no group columns, NULL or empty. The issues CSVs always hold all the run's group columns.

lineage

NULL, or the provider's raw values of the cells the pipeline changed: a data.frame or the path of a CSV file with the columns table_name, record_pk, column_name, raw_value and raw_source, as gpq_classify_issues() takes it in evidence. A listed cell's raw value shows beside its issue among the issues to act on, in its own unit's report only, and only where the record's key is given and, written as text, matches no other record's in its table.

lang, row_cap, example_cap, cell_cap

The reports' language (lang) and caps: the most rows a table shows (row_cap), examples per check (example_cap) and characters of delivered text per cell (cell_cap). Each NULL takes the run's rule set, then the option, then the built-in value (see groundplotqc_options); a value given here wins.

text

NULL, or a table of report text with the columns text_id, lang and text, whose rows stand in for the package's rows of the same text_id and lang.

Value

The files written, invisibly: a character vector of their paths, each named by its report unit (by the run ID for a run with no group columns). A run with group columns whose metadata/run.csv lists no unit gets no file, and an empty vector.

Details

Every issue must have a class before the results are written: run gpq_classify_issues(), which needs no evidence, then gpq_write_results() to output_dir. A run that stopped at pre-flight is refused, since it has no reports to build. A build first removes the reports and issues CSVs an earlier build wrote in the run's folder, never reports/preflight.html or the run's own tables. Each file is written under a temporary name and renamed when complete, so a build that stops leaves no partly written file.

One report and one CSV is built for each report unit metadata/run.csv lists, even a unit with no issue. An issue goes to its own unit's report. An issue of a check that checks whole tables or columns, with "*" as its unit and not marked reaches_other_unit, goes to every unit, and so does a results row that counts no records, such as a check that couldn't run because a table wasn't given. Any other issue or results row with "*" as its unit, a whole-column issue of records included, goes to no unit's report, and so does an issue the run marks reaches_other_unit (one holding a value read from another unit's records or from records with no unit). In a run of one unit, all of these go to that unit's report. A run with no group columns builds one report, reports/report.html, and one CSV, tables/report_issues.csv, holding every issue.

Each provider's file name is its unit value, with every character other than an ASCII letter, a digit, "-", "_" or "." written as % and its UTF-8 bytes in uppercase hex ("%" itself as %25). A leading or trailing "." is encoded too, and so is the first character of a value whose part before its first "." is a Windows reserved name such as CON, NUL or COM1 ("CON" becomes "%43ON"). So is the first character of a value that, whatever its case, is the name of one of the run's own files ("preflight", "national_summary", "report", "results", "issues" or "corrections"), so a provider's file never replaces one of them. Any value then makes a safe file name that decodes back.

The CSV has one row per issue sent to the unit, open and not evaluated, codes as stored. Its columns, in order: the group columns and the problem unit's key column; the table, column, check, severity and class; the check's text in the run language; the key's parts as key_<label> columns, named from the lineage spec's labels and empty where a key can't be split back exactly (a raw, fallback or no-lineage-spec key); then provider_key and provider_key_status; the record ID, value and expected value; proposed_value and easy_fix, empty until proposals exist; status, change, fingerprint and record count. Rows are sorted as the report's tables are. It is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark. In the provider's CSV, a text cell that starts with =, +, @, a tab or a carriage return, or with - where the cell isn't a number, is written with an apostrophe before it, so a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running it as a formula. reaches_other_unit isn't written.

Tables show at most row_cap rows and example_cap examples per check, and text longer than cell_cap characters is cut and ends with an ellipsis. The issues CSV has every issue, with its text in full.

See also

gpq_write_results(), which saves the run first; gpq_classify_issues(), which gives the issues their classes; gpq_decode_lineage(), which gives them provider keys.

Examples

# MAGPlot's bundled specification has known pre-flight warnings, so this warning is expected.
results <- gpq_check_conformance(
  magp_example, magp_spec(),
  group_cols = c("magp_contributor_id", "jurisdiction", "magp_dataset_id"),
  problem_unit = list("magp_plots", "magp_plot_id"), rules = magp_rules(), layers = 0:2
)
#> Warning: Pre-flight found 32 warning(s); see the returned table.
gpq_classify_issues(results$issues, magp_rules())
output <- tempfile("runs")
gpq_write_results(results, output)
files <- gpq_build_reports(results, output)
basename(files)
#> [1] "100.html"       "100_issues.csv" "110.html"       "110_issues.csv"
